what: parseApiDateTime: every message date goes through DateTime.tryParse (a RegExp + int.tryParse inside the SDK), then _hasExplicitTimeZone (second RegExp) and a DateTime.utc() rebuild; called from ApiMessage.fromJson/ChatSummary.fromJson for every field of every message
why_hot: encrypted_message_cache.dart:335 maps up to 2000 messages through ApiMessage.fromJson on the UI isolate AFTER the isolate returned (decrypt+jsonDecode are inside _runCompute, fromJson is not; maxLimit=2000 at :236); history catch-up decodes pages repeatedly (backend_chat_provider.dart:2610,3223,3358); cold inbox start parses 2-3 dates per chat (ChatSummary.lastActivity/pinnedAt + lastMessage). Measured: DateTime.tryParse = 32 us, parseApiDateTime = 22.9 us/date x 2000 = 45.8 ms; with edited_at up to ~92 ms, plus jsonDecode 12.6 ms
est_gain: 2000-message restore: 46-92 ms -> 3-5 ms (batch FFI, ~30x). Measured on JIT desktop; AOT/mobile multiplier typically 1.5-3x worse for Dart, so the absolute saving is larger
risk: low boundary (String -> int64 epoch micros + hasOffset flag, ~24 bytes, FFI call ~0.3-1 us), but batch API is mandatory or 2000 calls eat the win; must reproduce the 'no timezone -> treat as UTC' branch exactly or every sort/date separator shifts; WEB: no dart:ffi, and compute/Isolate.run on web runs on the same thread, so this is one of the few places where Rust->wasm is the only real speed-up rather than a thread-offload

what: messagePreviewText: builds a fresh md.Document with the full GitHub-flavored extension set, parses to an AST, walks it into a StringBuffer and collapses whitespace with a RegExp - per chat preview, synchronously inside the itemBuilder of the inbox list
why_hot: chat_list_screen.dart:1334-1348 calls it from the row builder of every visible chat (via MessagePreviewFormatter, cache 512 at :48-59); the cache is empty on cold start (:464 clears it on account/filter change) so the first inbox screen costs 15 visible rows x 162 us, and scrolling 200 chats ~32 ms; cache:false for secret chats (:1416) parses on every rebuild. Measured: 40 us for 7 chars, 162 us for 153 chars, 473 us for 444 chars; 128 us of that is parseLines alone
est_gain: 15-row inbox: 2.4 ms -> ~0.1 ms; 200 chats: ~32 ms -> ~1 ms. Batch API over the visible window (Vec<String> in, one buffer + offsets out)
risk: pulldown-cmark is not the same GFM dialect as package:markdown, and the preview sits next to the full text in the list, so divergences on tables/footnotes/HTML will be visible; safest scope is 'strip markup + collapse whitespace' only; strings copy both ways (~153 B per row, negligible) but the API must be batched; WEB needs a wasm backend (an isolate cannot help on web, where compute is same-thread)

what: DocxParser.parseBytes: ZipDecoder inflates the whole archive, utf8-decodes word/document.xml, then one dotAll lazy RegExp with a backreference walks the entire XML, with 2 more RegExps per paragraph, 1 per run and 5 sequential replaceAll per text node (_unescapeXml) - all synchronous on the UI isolate
why_hot: native_file_viewer_screen.dart:608-618: _parse() in initState calls parseBytes synchronously, setState(_isLoading=false) only afterwards, so tapping a .docx attachment freezes the UI with no progress indicator. Already listed in audit/perf/00-summary.md as 'requires profiler' (50-200 KB docs). Measured on a 610 KB document.xml: outer regex 8 ms + 13 ms per 1000 paragraphs (3000 -> ~39 ms) + 3.4 ms inflate ~ 50 ms/MB
est_gain: 5-20 ms for a 50-200 KB docx today, 50 ms/MB; compute() removes it from the frame entirely. Rust (inflate + quick-xml, no regex) would cut the work itself to 2-5 ms and also help web, but the document opens once per file
risk: low for compute(): Uint8List in, plain List<DocxBlock> out, one copy; WEB: compute on web is same-thread, so the isolate fix buys nothing there (the 5-20 ms stay, only the blocked frame moves). Rust here is only worth it as part of a real docx reader (styles, lists, tables, images), not for this regex parser

what: _content.split('\n') runs inside build() of the plain-text viewer (re-executed on every search keystroke, wrap toggle and theme change), and itemBuilder lowercases each visible line on every build
why_hot: onChanged: (val) => setState(() => _searchQuery = ...) at :912-913 rebuilds on every typed character, and :926 rebuilds on the wrap toggle; the viewer opens arbitrary chat attachments with no size cap. Measured: split of a 1 MB / 20k-line text = 3.85 ms, toLowerCase of 1 MB = 5.55 ms -> a 5 MB log costs ~20 ms of main-thread work per keystroke (keyboard feels sticky); already in perf P1 #18 for the split, this adds the per-line lowercase
est_gain: 1 MB: 3.85 ms per rebuild -> 0 by splitting once at load and keeping a match index; Rust on UTF-8 offsets would be ~0.3 ms/MB, the only path that also helps web
risk: isolate returns List<String> (20-100k objects) which is copied across the boundary - better to return one text buffer + Int32List offsets; WEB: compute is same-thread so only the caching part helps there; FFI would need the same flat buffer shape

what: customEmojiLength: replaceAll(RegExp, replacement) over the whole draft (always allocates a new string even with zero matches) plus a full grapheme segmentation via package:characters, run as a TextInputFormatter on every keystroke and again in build() for the counter
evidence:
int customEmojiLength(String text) =>
    text.replaceAll(customEmojiPattern, '\uFFFC').characters.length;
...
      !newValue.composing.isCollapsed ||
          customEmojiLength(newValue.text) <= maximum
      ? newValue
      : oldValue;
why_hot: CustomEmojiLengthFormatter is on inputFormatters for comments with a 10000 limit (post_comments_screen.dart:472-473), post creation with 4096 (create_post_screen.dart:869-870, plus a second call in build() at :935 for the counter), interactive composer (180/100/500). Measured: 294 us per call on 8400 code units, 245 us of which is replaceAll
est_gain: 294 us -> ~30-80 us with Rust grapheme counting, but a one-line Dart guard (if (text.length <= maximum) return value, since code units >= graphemes) removes the cost for almost every keystroke
risk: a plugin for a 0.3 ms operation is not worth an FFI + wasm build; grapheme tables must match package:characters exactly (Unicode version) or the limit stops matching what the UI shows

what: Every incoming message re-sorts the whole chat list (updated.sort(compareChatRecency)) and the inbox screen rebuilds its full projection: two List.of copies, filter, indexWhere for the saved chat and a Map<int,int> idToIndex of all chats
why_hot: the websocket push path (backend_chat_provider _onMessage) calls this for every message of every chat, including group chats at a few messages per second, and chatsProvider drives the whole inbox screen; an incremental insertSorted(updated, chat, compareChatRecency) already exists at :1150 but is used on only one of seven paths. Cost: ~0.2 ms at 200 chats, ~2-3 ms per message at 2000
est_gain: 0.2-3 ms per incoming message removed by making the update incremental; Rust cannot help (sorting 2000 pointers through FFI costs more than Dart's in-place sort with DateTime.compareTo)
risk: no FFI risk because it is not a Rust case; the projection must stay keyed by chat identity or the list flickers

what: DebouncedSearchNotifier.search runs the local pass synchronously on every keystroke: per chat three toLowerCase().contains() allocations (name/username/lastMessage.content) and per feed post three more, one of them over the full post body; only the backend request is debounced
why_hot: contacts_screen.dart:523 and chat_members_screen.dart:109 call search(q) directly from onChanged; the feed pass (search_provider.dart:92-98) lowercases post.content of every loaded post. Measured: toLowerCase costs 5.55 ms/MB, so 200 posts x ~1 KB ~ 1.1 ms plus 600 string allocations per keystroke
est_gain: 0.5-1.5 ms per keystroke; removed by debouncing the local pass and storing a normalized copy next to the model
risk: an isolate per keystroke is worse (round trip + reordering); a Rust inverted index would only pay off if local full-text search over history is ever added (message search is server-side today)

what: Each feed card constructs MarkdownBody + a new CustomEmojiSyntax instance (which owns its own RegExp) + a new builders map inside build(); flutter_markdown_plus re-parses only when data changes, so the cost lands on card mount
evidence:
final markdown = MarkdownBody(
      data: post.content,
      inlineSyntaxes: [CustomEmojiSyntax()],
      builders: {'nios-emoji': CustomEmojiMarkdownBuilder()},
      // Cached in didChangeDependencies: fromTheme() builds dozens of styles.
      styleSheet: _markdownStyle,
why_hot: the feed mounts cards while scrolling; a post over 400 chars is parsed into an AST and then into a widget tree, on top of image decoding in the same frame; the stylesheet part is already fixed (cached in didChangeDependencies), the syntax/builder allocation is not
est_gain: 0.2-1 ms per mounted card; the markdown parse could move to Rust but the result is a widget/InlineSpan tree, so the win is eaten by rebuilding it in Dart
risk: moving markdown parsing to Rust does not remove widget construction, which dominates; the only cheap fix is hoisting the syntax/builder instances, and that is Dart-only

what: QrImageView recomputes the QR matrix in build() (QrValidator.validate -> QrCode.fromData: bit stream + Reed-Solomon + version check); the page also watches chatsProvider without select, so it rebuilds on every incoming message of the account
evidence:
child: QrImageView(
                              data: _pairCode!,
                              size: constraints.maxWidth.clamp(0, 210),
...
    final chats = ref.watch(chatsProvider).value ?? const [];
why_hot: _contactSection() at :580 reads chatsProvider unselected (already perf P1 #14) and _reveal('pair-code', QrImageView) is in the same build() tree, so every message anywhere regenerates the pairing QR while that page is open; qr_flutter 4.1.0 has no internal cache and QrImageView.withQr is not used
est_gain: ~100-200 us per message for a version 2-5 QR; fixed by computing QrCode.fromData once in initState and passing QrImageView.withQr, plus a select on the provider
risk: no FFI risk; a Rust QR encoder (rcq/fast_qr) would be ~50x faster but on a single short payload it is a micro-optimisation with no scale

what: Image resize/JPEG re-encode before upload is already delegated to the platform: FlutterImageCompress.compressWithList / compressAndGetFile (Android native, Windows native, flutter_image_compress_web on web); the Dart side only decides whether to compress at all
evidence:
final Uint8List result = await FlutterImageCompress.compressWithList(
        bytes,
        minWidth: maxWidth ?? _maxWidth,
        minHeight: maxHeight ?? _maxHeight,
        quality: quality,
        format: CompressFormat.jpeg,
      );
why_hot: called from account_profile_section.dart:176, create_post_screen.dart:174 and :449 for every avatar/photo upload; the heavy work is already off the Dart isolate
est_gain: none - a Rust JPEG codec would be a regression against a native platform encoder and would add a wasm backend for web
risk: adding Rust here means shipping our own JPEG encoder and a second web code path for something the platform already does in native/hardware code
